title: Gender Violence, Gender Justice and Gender-Based Laws: An Analysis of Pattern and Policies in India and Indonesia
affiliations: University of Delhi - University of Delhi, Campus Law Centre, Students

detail.title: Gender Violence, Gender Justice and Gender-Based Laws: An Analysis of Pattern and Policies in India and Indonesia

keywords: Poor Implementation of Laws and Policies
Right to Equality and Non-Discrimination in India and Indonesia

detail.abstract: If we look at the status of women in a particular society, we can get a fair idea about its social organization and standard. Violence against women is a challenge against the right to equality and an extreme form of violation of human rights. From ancient times to the modern era, women face discrimination, exploitation, and violence in every walk of their life, and this phenomenon is prevalent across all borders. Every civilized society tries to protect its members both in public and private spaces with the help of a set of laws and rights. Hosts of laws and beneficial legislation enacted to ameliorate women's condition have failed to achieve the desired purpose due several factors. Thus mere enactment of laws will not serve the desired purpose until they are effectively implemented and assertively claimed by women. This paper presents a comparative analysis of the various forms of gender violence and the status of the gender-based laws that are enacted for achieving gender justice in India and Indonesia. It analyses the extent to which these women favoring laws of both countries prevent the frequency of the occurrence of gender violence and some recommendations for bringing about changes to this situation.

title: Social Anxiety and Safety Behaviours in Indian Females Who Stutter
affiliations: Era University, ERA University, ERA University and King George's Medical University

detail.title: Social Anxiety and Safety Behaviours in Indian Females Who Stutter

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study was performed in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki. This human study was approved by Era's Lucknow Medical College & Hospital, Era University, Lucknow - approval: ECR/717/Inst./up/2015/RR-21. All adult participants provided written informed consent to participate in this study. Written informed consent was obtained from the individual(s) for publication of the details of their medical case.

detail.abstract:
Background

People who stutter often face both speech difficulties and social challenges. In stressful social situations, they resort to safety behaviours to cope with anxiety. However, these behaviours can worsen anxiety over time and lead to less effective treatment outcomes. Research on females is limited due to higher childhood recovery rates, leading to a male-to-female ratio of 4:1 among adults. Negligible information is available on Indian females with persistent stuttering.

Aim

This study explores the relationship between social anxiety and the frequency of safety behaviours among Indian females who stutter.

Methods
Ten females who visited King George’s Medical University, Lucknow, for stuttering treatment participated in the study. The Liebowitz Social Anxiety Scale assessed their social anxiety, and the Safety Behaviour Checklist 2023 assessed the usage frequency of specific safety behaviours during social encounters. Correlations were established between the frequency of safety behaviour and the pretreatment score of social anxiety.

Results
The results showed that all ten participants experienced high levels of social anxiety and frequently used safety behaviours. Most safety behaviours were found to be positively correlated with social anxiety, except for a few.

Conclusion
The present study suggests a strong connection between social anxiety and the use of safety behaviours in females who stutter. However, a few exceptions indicate that some safety behaviours may have different underlying factors.

title: Metals, Markets and Melting Points: Deriving Market
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Metals, Markets and Melting Points: Deriving Market
detail.abstract: We derive information on changes in market expectations of global warming from the historical prices of copper, nickel and cobalt. These commodities are critical components of technologies (e.g., solar panels and electric batteries) that are likely to play a role in reducing emissions, and for which demand is likely to increase under net-zero transition. We model the value of these commodities as a function of future global temperatures and fit the modelled value of commodities to those observed historically. We use a sign-restricted VAR model to isolate the changes in commodity prices that are due to changes in expectations of climate transition. We find that market expectations of global warming have decreased slightly by around 0.3°C since 2010. Market-implied uncertainty around expectations of global temperatures has also increased in recent years.

title: Climate Change and Resource Competition in a Multipolar World
affiliations: The University of Edinburgh

detail.title: Climate Change and Resource Competition in a Multipolar World

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There is no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, patient data, or clinical trials; therefore, ethical approval was not required.

detail.abstract: This paper explores the intersection of climate change, resource competition, and global security in an emerging multipolar order. It argues that climate change has become increasingly securitized, producing direct implications for water scarcity, food insecurity, and fragile supply chains. The study introduces three conceptual innovations: Climate Multipolarity (a fragmented and multi-centered climate governance system), Resource Tipping Points (critical thresholds in water, energy, food, and rare earth elements that trigger irreversible crises), and Security Ecology (a hybrid and networked architecture involving states, regional organizations, corporations, cities, and transnational coalitions). Case studies of the Nile Basin, the Mekong River, Arctic geopolitics, and the Sahel, combined with scenario projections for 2035-2050, show that multipolarity simultaneously creates opportunities for more inclusive governance and risks of intensified fragmentation. The conclusion outlines policy options, including reform of the UN Security Council, NATO's adaptation, regional-global bridges, and new forms of multilateralism for resource sharing. This study contributes to international relations and security studies by reframing climate security as a systemic challenge within an increasingly multipolar world.

title: Trademark Use in Flux: Bridging Legal Doctrine and Commercial Realities
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Trademark Use in Flux: Bridging Legal Doctrine and Commercial Realities
detail.abstract:
Contemporary business has challenged the legal view of trademarks, and courts have tried to align this reality with the law. One of the purported solutions to this new challenge is formulating a "trademark use" doctrine. This thesis analyses the "trademark use" doctrine, contending that its application lacks foundation in both legislative history and statutory language. It challenges the doctrine's continued relevance in light of contemporary commercial realities.

The article argues that “trademark use,” as conceptualised, fails to present any meaningful innovation in addressing current trademark conflicts. Rather, its rigid, formalistic approach is at odds with modern commerce. It also posits that strict adherence to the doctrine does not improve courts’ capacity to resolve disputes in a way that appropriately balances the competing interests of trademark owners and the public. Instead, the likelihood of confusion (LoC) test, long entrenched in U.S. trademark jurisprudence, and fair use serve as a more flexible and effective mechanism for resolving disputes. The article concludes by stating that the focus on “trademark use” is mainly superfluous and may impede the efficient resolution of disputes, undermining economic efficiency and free expression. Courts can achieve the necessary balance by applying the LoC tests and fair use doctrine. These existing frameworks are sufficiently adaptable to address the nuanced demands of modern commerce. The article suggests the need for further empirical research on courts’ responses to novel and borderline cases to understand the judicial attitude toward “trademark use” and why the doctrine has not delivered on all its promises.

title: A Practical Framework for Retail and Quantitative Traders to Analyze Spoofing in Limit Order Books
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: A Practical Framework for Retail and Quantitative Traders to Analyze Spoofing in Limit Order Books

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no financial or personal relationships with other people or organizations that could inappropriately influence or be perceived to influence the work presented in this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants, patient data, or sensitive personal information. All analyses were conducted using publicly available market data, and no ethics committee approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was conducted without external funding. The author independently designed the study, developed the framework, and performed all analysis.

detail.abstract: Spoofing-placing deceptive orders in the limit order book to manipulate price signals-has become a growing concern with the rise of high-frequency and algorithmic trading. While regulatory bodies and exchanges deploy advanced detection algorithms, retail traders and quantitative learners often lack robust tools or frameworks to study and analyze spoofing activity. This paper synthesizes academic theory, empirical evidence, and practical insights, and presents a framework that enables retail traders and quantitative learners to collect data, compute relevant metrics, and model spoofing behavior for research and experimentation. Note: This paper was written in April 2025. Submission to SSRN/arXiv occurs in August 2025.

title: "Short Communication on Dignity in the Digital Age"
affiliations: Qur'anic Covenant Research Centre (QCRC)

detail.title: "Short Communication on Dignity in the Digital Age"
detail.abstract: In a world where our lives are increasingly digitised, the sacredness of human dignity—so profoundly embedded in Qur'anic ethics—is often tested by the tools we use. From online surveillance to silent data theft, we're facing a catastrophe not just of technology, but of values. This article examines how incivility in the digital world, characterised by a disregard for privacy and consent, erodes human dignity. It incorporates the Qur'an’s guidance, as seen in Surah Al-Hujurat's call against spying, with contemporary laws such as Pakistan's Personal Data Protection Bill, California's CCPA, the UDHR, and the ICCPR. However, alas, the crux remains: laws can not fix what we as humans are not willing to acknowledge. Until we internalise the worth of every human being, our digital spaces will remain invasive and pejorative.

title: Beyond Profit Maximization: Dealer Metrics and Tradeoffs in RFQ Bond Markets
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Technical University of Denmark, University of Copenhagen and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Beyond Profit Maximization: Dealer Metrics and Tradeoffs in RFQ Bond Markets
detail.abstract: Classical approaches to market making focus primarily on profit maximization. However, real-world dealers face more complex decisions and incorporate additional metrics and pricing strategies. In this study, we conduct an empirical analysis of the Request-for-Quote (RFQ) protocol in a bond market setting, evaluating various machine learning-based market making agent formulations under dealer-relevant metrics such as hit ratio, distance-to-cover, distance-to-target, and distance-to-win. We find that quantile-based agents, which explicitly target desired hit ratios, match profit-maximizing agents on spread profit and distance-to-cover, while outperforming them on distance-to-target and distance-to-win. Moreover, these agents offer greater flexibility, enabling alignment with external constraints such as dealer-specific hit ratio targets. Incorporating post-trade prices further improves performance across most metrics. We also establish a connection between key dealer metrics and the structure of the quantile loss function. These results underscore the importance of non-profit objectives and quantile-based loss functions in the design of effective market making strategies.

title: Reflective Admission Model (RAM): Institutionalising Self-Reflection to Improve Fairness in Dispute Resolution
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Reflective Admission Model (RAM): Institutionalising Self-Reflection to Improve Fairness in Dispute Resolution
detail.abstract: Fairness is a persistent concern in dispute resolution. While existing models emphasise mediator neutrality and procedural safeguards, less attention has been given to how disputants themselves shape fairness perceptions through the ways they frame conflict. This working paper introduces the Reflective Admission Model (RAM), a new theory and intake protocol designed to institutionalise self-reflection at the earliest stage of dispute resolution. RAM requires parties to complete two structured reflections: (1) My Contribution-a brief acknowledgment of one's own role in the escalation of conflict; and (2) Sequence & Provocation-a timeline that clarifies actions and triggers. Mediators then use these reflections to establish fairness norms during dialogue. By embedding self-reflection into intake processes, RAM reduces overreliance on mediator skill alone and strengthens perceptions of impartiality, accountability, and balance. Safeguards ensure that reflections remain confidential, voluntary, and non-punitive. Preliminary workshops indicate that RAM enhances trust in mediator neutrality, fosters shared responsibility, and lowers perceptions of bias. A proposed randomised controlled trial will test RAM against conventional protocols. RAM contributes to theory by reframing fairness as not only procedural and relational but also reflective. For practice, it provides mediators with a simple, low-cost intervention to improve fairness perceptions. For institutions, it offers a scalable design innovation. The model invites critique, adaptation, and empirical testing across mediation, restorative justice, and peacebuilding contexts.

title: Hashtag Politics: The Role of Twitter (X) in Shaping Political Narratives in Pakistan
affiliations: Qurtuba University of Science and Information Technology, Students, Shirkat Gah Women's Resource Centre, District Youth Officer, Sports and Youth Dept, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, The value Engineering Pakistan, University of Haripur, Abdul Wali Khan University, Head Current Affairs, PTV National Peshawar and Ex MPA and President PTI Women Wing Malakand Region, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa

detail.title: Hashtag Politics: The Role of Twitter (X) in Shaping Political Narratives in Pakistan
detail.abstract: In recent years, Twitter (now X) has emerged as a powerful tool for shaping political narratives in Pakistan. Political leaders, parties, journalists, and citizens increasingly use hashtags to frame issues, mobilize supporters, and influence public opinion. These digital conversations often spill over into mainstream media, amplifying their reach and impact. Hashtag politics in Pakistan has become a dynamic arena where competing narratives ranging from governance performance and corruption allegations to nationalism and electoral campaigns are contested in real time. The platform enables both top-down political messaging and bottom-up grassroots activism, fostering political engagement across diverse demographics. However, it also intensifies political polarization, spreads disinformation, and reinforces echo chambers. This study examines the evolving role of Twitter in Pakistan's political landscape, highlighting how the strategic use of hashtags can both strengthen democratic participation and shape the direction of national political discourse.

title: Semantodynamics: Thermodynamics of Semantics

detail.title: Semantodynamics: Thermodynamics of Semantics
detail.abstract: Semantodynamics posits that semantic activity—meaning formation, flow, and relevance—evolves as a thermodynamic gradient system on a structured state space. We axiomatize a core semantic state (S,σ,gV,T) (S,\sigma,g_V,T), define the flux B=σ∇S (B=\sigma\nabla S), and introduce a free-energy functional whose Euler–Lagrange and continuity laws yield observable balance. Classical engines—Linear Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics (LNET), elliptic variational theory, spectral geometry, Optimal Transport (OT), Information Bottleneck (IB), and KL-control—are unified as layers of one variational grammar. We prove three flagship theorems (reciprocity, coherence bounds, control–information bridge) and provide measurement-ready protocols for empirical validation in real corpora. The result is a foundational and operational framework for quantifying, controlling, and designing semantic systems—including discourse and LLM generation—under principled thermodynamic constraints.

title: Role of Diplostomum Genetic Variability in Host Immune Response Modulation in Nile Tilapia
affiliations: LADOKE AKINTOLA UNIVERSITY OF TECHNOLOGY OGBOMOSO, NIGERIA

detail.title: Role of Diplostomum Genetic Variability in Host Immune Response Modulation in Nile Tilapia
detail.abstract: This article provides a comprehensive synthesis of the current understanding of the host-parasite relationship between the digenean trematode Diplostomum and its second intermediate host, the Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus). It examines the significant economic threat posed by Diplostomum in aquaculture and delves into the complex interplay between the parasite's genetic variability and the host's immune response. The report details the parasite's complex, multi-host life cycle and its pathological effects on fish, including cataract formation and reduced growth. It reviews the innate and adaptive immune systems of teleost fish and explores how parasite-specific genotypes can modulate host immunity. By synthesizing findings from diverse studies, this analysis elucidates how the parasite's ability to rapidly migrate to an "immune-privileged site" and actively suppress or modulate host defenses is a key survival strategy. The report highlights the critical knowledge gaps regarding this specific host-parasite system and proposes future research directions, emphasizing the need for a targeted, integrated management approach that accounts for the underlying genetic and immunological dynamics to protect the vital Nile tilapia industry.

title: Deep Interpretability for AGI Decision Systems: Making Superintelligent Reasoning Comprehensible
affiliations: Vishwakarma Institute of Technology

detail.title: Deep Interpretability for AGI Decision Systems: Making Superintelligent Reasoning Comprehensible
detail.abstract: As artificial general intelligence (AGI) systems approach and potentially exceed human cognitive capabilities, the challenge of understanding their decision-making processes becomes increasingly critical for safety, trust, and responsible deployment. This paper presents a comprehensive framework for deep interpretability in AGI decision systems, addressing the fundamental challenge of making superintelligent reasoning comprehensible to human operators and stakeholders. We propose a multi-layered interpretability architecture that combines advanced explanation techniques, hierarchical reasoning decomposition, and real-time transparency mechanisms specifically designed for AGI-level systems. Our framework introduces novel approaches including Recursive Reasoning Decomposition (RRD), Hierarchical Attention Visualization (HAV), and Dynamic Interpretability Scaling (DIS) to address the unique challenges posed by superintelligent AI systems. Through theoretical analysis and empirical validation using scaled transformer architectures, we demonstrate that our approach maintains interpretability even as system capabilities scale beyond human-level performance. The proposed framework provides actionable insights for AGI safety researchers, system designers, and policymakers working to ensure transparent and accountable artificial general intelligence.

title: Economic Complexity: Promise and Potential for Sustainable Development Decision Support
affiliations: KU Leuven - Department of Economics, KU Leuven - Center for Economic Studies and University of British Columbia (UBC) - School of Engineering

detail.title: Economic Complexity: Promise and Potential for Sustainable Development Decision Support

declarations.declarationOfInterest: On behalf of all authors, the corresponding author states that there is no conflict of interest.

detail.abstract: The 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are at the heart of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and provide a comprehensive framework for societal progress and planetary health. It is abundantly clear, however, that many countries face challenges in achieving these goals and the world is still a long way from making sustainable development a global reality. Insights from economic complexity theory can help to better understand and support the journey to sustainable development. Economic complexity is a rapidly moving field with numerous developments, applications, and promises. Despite this, many misconceptions and overstatements in the field remain. This article provides a detailed, critical overview of the status quo to identify what is needed to unlock the full potential of economic complexity-based sustainability-oriented decision support.

title: Drawing and Scheduling the UEFA Champions League League Phase
affiliations: Ecole Nationale des Ponts et Chaussées (ENPC), Ecole Nationale des Ponts et Chaussées (ENPC), Ecole Nationale des Ponts et Chaussées (ENPC) and Ecole Nationale des Ponts et Chaussées (ENPC)

detail.title: Drawing and Scheduling the UEFA Champions League League Phase
detail.abstract: The new league phase of the UEFA Champions League (UCL), introduced in the 2024-25 season, gathers 36 soccer teams that are ranked in a single table and play an incomplete round-robin. Each team faces only eight opponents that are randomly drawn, subject to seeding pot and association constraints. We investigate four methods for drawing the league phase matchups. First, we consider the official draw procedure used by UEFA, which we call Draw matchups first, where matchups are drawn before the match schedule is built. We show, using a chromatic index argument from graph theory, that the scheduling issue cannot be ignored when drawing the matchups, by exhibiting a draw outcome which satisfies all the pot and association constraints but is noncompact, i.e., cannot be scheduled within the allocated eight match days. Second, we study an alternative method, which we call Build schedule first, where one first builds a schedule template satisfying pot constraints before randomly populating it with the 36 teams. We show that the minimum number of breaks is equal to 4 and explicitly build a schedule that minimizes the number of breaks and optimizes various fairness and attractiveness criteria. For both methods, we consider a randomized variant where the order of pots from which teams and their opponents are drawn, for the first method, and the order we follow to populate the schedule template, for the second method, are randomized. We implement the four methods using integer programming to express the draw constraints, and run Monte Carlo simulations to compare them in the case of the 2024-25 UCL and the 2024-25 UEFA Europa League (UEL), which follows the exact same rules. We assess the fairness of the four methods by comparing the distributions of average opponent strength that they produce for the 36 teams. We also measure the impact of the four procedures on the matchup probabilities. All four procedures are fair to all teams-no team is significantly aggrieved-and the Draw matchups first procedures yield more uniform matchup probabilities than the Build schedule first ones. Finally, we introduce a luck index that objectively ranks teams from the luckiest to the unluckiest during the actual draw. As interesting asides, we provide examples of noncompact draw outcomes and derive the minimum number of scheduling breaks for general setups with p seeding pots, q teams per pot, and where each team faces k opponents from each pot, and we prove the absence of a cut vertex in the UEFA Conference League draw graph. The Julia code is available at https://julienguyon.github.io/UEFA-league-phase-draw.

title: The Limits of Free Utilities: Evidence from South Africa
affiliations: ETH Zürich - CER-ETH - Center of Economic Research at ETH Zurich

detail.title: The Limits of Free Utilities: Evidence from South Africa
detail.abstract: Electricity and water use have the potential to improve the welfare of poor households in developing countries. I evaluate the impact of eligibility for the Indigent Program, a South African policy that provided a certain amount of free electricity and water to households with incomes lower than a cut-off, using two household-level survey datasets and a regression discontinuity design. I find null effects of the policy on electricity and water expenditure and use, as well as on appliance ownership. The mechanism behind this finding is likely that eligibility failed to augment program take-up. Policy implications relate to increasing program awareness, dismantling administrative and financial barriers, and infrastructure investments to improve access to electricity and water.

title: Deepfake Diplomacy and International Relations: Assessing the Impact of AI-Generated Media on Global Trust, Diplomatic Engagement, and Conflict Escalation
affiliations: Qurtuba University of Science and Information Technology, Students, University of South Asia, Advocate Lahore High Court, Army Public School, Cyprus International University and Central University of Punjab

detail.title: Deepfake Diplomacy and International Relations: Assessing the Impact of AI-Generated Media on Global Trust, Diplomatic Engagement, and Conflict Escalation
detail.abstract: This paper examines the new possibilities that deepfakes will have in defining the course of diplomacy and international relations. It studies the impact of deepfakes on diplomatic trust, leadership legitimacy, conflict escalation, and normalization of disinformation through a qualitative research design conducted through Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA). It was concluded that deepfakes are drivers of diplomatic suspicion, are used to undermine the credibility of leaders, and are a channel of increasing misinformation through media logics. The study highlights the importance of creating global verification systems, the need to increase digital diplomat literacy, and multilateral regulation against AI-fueled disinformation. The final message is that deepfakes are a serious communicative and political challenge that disrupts trust in international relations.

title: Indian Perspective on Arbitrability of Insolvency Disputes: Intersection, Intervention and Interpretation for Synergy among Both Regimes
affiliations: University of Delhi - University of Delhi, Campus Law Centre, Students

detail.title: Indian Perspective on Arbitrability of Insolvency Disputes: Intersection, Intervention and Interpretation for Synergy among Both Regimes
detail.abstract: India is fast emerging as a vibrant economy committed to establishing itself as a business-friendly destination country. The current ranking in the World Economic Forum and various reforms to modify the Indian regulatory framework exhibit this trend. From ranking in to in in "ease of doing business", the constant effort towards improving Indian business regulation by adopting best practices is observable. In this regard, the Indian laws on Insolvency, Bankruptcy and Arbitration provide swift insolvency resolution and better settlement of disputes outside the traditional and cumbersome court procedures. However, both laws have several confrontational zones of overlapping that require emphasis. The focus and purpose of the paper are to analyze the interplay between arbitration and insolvency proceedings. Further, the case analysis will highlight the legal position of courts and adjudicatory authorities about the conditions when both regimes can continue concurrently to protect the creditor dealing with an insolvent individual or body. The main idea is to strive and find ways to avoid a collision between the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (hereinafter IBC) and Arbitration and Conciliation Act (hereinafter A&C Act,) with an appreciation of the applicability, interface, and issues regarding the arbitrability of insolvency proceedings. The paper qualitatively examined several judicial pronouncements relevant to different aspects of the A&C Act and IBC. The results deduced from the case analysis suggest that the insolvency and arbitration overlap is inevitable due to grey areas and recommend that until the Indian jurisprudence matures, the arbitrability of insolvency disputes will continue. The paper will aid in devising precise and novel ways to balance diverse conflicts and devising novel ways to balance these conflicts to secure the best from both these regimes.

title: Artificial Intelligence and the Fight Against Misinformation: Analyzing the Role of Digital Media in Shaping Public Perceptions in Pakistan
affiliations: Excise and Taxation officer, Abdul Wali Khan University, Qurtuba University of Science and Information Technology, Students and Allama Iqbal Open University

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Fight Against Misinformation: Analyzing the Role of Digital Media in Shaping Public Perceptions in Pakistan
detail.abstract: The study investigates the impact of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI and deepfakes on the creation and proliferation of misinformation in Pakistan and the role of digital media ecosystems in cementing perceptions. The paper employs qualitative content analysis of 300 items (news articles, social-media posts, fact-checks, and civil-society reports) in the year 20232025 to identify priority areas of AI-enabled misinformation flows, platform affordances that can fuel misinformed content, and the ability of local fact-checkers and civil-society actors and limited populace awareness of fake-content detectors. The results reveal an active disinformation economy with political motives, platform architecture, and poor digital literacy exacerbating the ills of AI-facilitated misinformation. What the paper recommends by way of policy is to address the issue of platform accountability, capacity building of the fact-checkers, and media literacy interventions that are context-sensitive to the Pakistani socio-political environment.

reference: Harvard Business School Technology & Operations Mgt. Unit Working Paper No. 26-012; Harvard Business School Working Paper No. 26-012
title: Reliable Switchback Experiments with Rerandomization for Auction Environments at Procter & Gamble
affiliations: Harvard Business School, Procter & Gamble and Harvard University - Technology & Operations Management Unit

detail.title: Reliable Switchback Experiments with Rerandomization for Auction Environments at Procter & Gamble

publicationDetails.detailsText: Harvard Business School Technology & Operations Mgt. Unit Working Paper No. 26-012
publicationDetails.journalName: Harvard Business School: Technology & Operations Management Unit Working Paper Series

publicationDetails.detailsText: Harvard Business School Working Paper No. 26-012

detail.abstract: Auction environments play an increasingly central role across industries such as transportation, commodities, and media. Companies like Procter & Gamble (P&G) rely on advanced digital solutions to optimize auction performance and must rigorously validate algorithmic changes before wide-scale deployment. Yet standard A/B testing methods are frequently infeasible in these settings because user randomization is not under the control of the auction seller. Switchback experiments, which randomize treatment assignment over discrete time periods, offer a practical alternative but often suffer from low statistical power and are further complicated by potential carryover effects, where previous treatments can affect current outcomes. This paper introduces a new rerandomization-based design that addresses both the issue of achieving adequate covariate balance and the challenges posed by carryover effects. Building on assignment paths from a completely randomized design, we measure covariate imbalance and only accept assignment schedules below a specified threshold, thus enhancing precision. We then propose an analytic adjustment for the practical scenario when the experiment has to be paused, treating disruptions—such as business parameter constraints or technical failures—as fixed yet unknown events that can be incorporated into the variance calibration. Through extensive numerical simulations mimicking real data from the auction environment, we show that our approach substantially boosts efficiency, remains robust to different choices of covariate sets and imbalance thresholds, and adapts well under assignment non-compliance. Since Jan 2025, P&G has integrated the new rerandomization strategy into its experimentation workflow—applying it to 70 experiments across five auction hypotheses in eight global markets. The results indicate a potential 10–20% sales lift and 5–15% cost savings. Beyond its immediate application to switchback experiments at P&G, the methodology underscores a broader principle in data-driven decision-making: carefully engineered randomization, combined with robust analytic strategies that account for real-world implementation challenges, can yield reliable and actionable insights even in complex operational contexts.

This Feature Comment (a) assesses the courts’ role in bid protest reform in light of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit’s en banc decision in Percipient.ai, (b) reviews the potential benefits of expanded debriefings, and (c) explains how agency-level bid protests could be reformed, using agencies’ own best practices, to make them more effective.

title: Retaining population with water? Irrigation policies and depopulation in Spain over the long term
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Universidad de Alcalá, University of Zaragoza, University of Zaragoza and University of Zaragoza

detail.title: Retaining population with water? Irrigation policies and depopulation in Spain over the long term

keywords.keywords: Irrigation programs - Depopulation - Place-based policies - Long-term view - Staggered DiD - Spain

detail.abstract: The diverse effects of irrigation are becoming a central focus of research. This paper evaluates the demographic impact of irrigation programs in Spain, a country historically characterized by the widespread implementation of irrigation infrastructure and pronounced regional population decline. As a form of place-based policy, irrigation has been credited with helping to retain, and even attract, population by shifting crop patterns toward more labor-intensive or higher-value varieties and enhancing agricultural productivity, thereby boosting competitiveness, which in turn can improve employment opportunities and living standards. However, the effects on population have not yet been assessed. We use a highly spatially disaggregated database at the municipality level, covering census years from 1950 to 2011, and implement a staggered difference-in-differences design exploiting variation in the timing of irrigation introduction. We address identification threats and conduct robustness checks. The findings show a positive and significant effect on population only for irrigation developments initiated between the 1950s and 1970s, with no effect for later periods. We discuss mechanisms and policy implications.

title: Innovative Learn-by-Doing Digital Education and Attitudes Towards STEM: An RCT in Italian High Schools
affiliations: IMT School for Advanced Studies Lucca, AXES Lab, European University Institute, University of Bologna and University of Brescia

detail.title: Innovative Learn-by-Doing Digital Education and Attitudes Towards STEM: An RCT in Italian High Schools
detail.abstract: We conducted a randomized controlled trial to test the effectiveness of creative STEM activities on the propensity to enroll in a STEM university course and career aspirations on a sample of 710 high school students in Italy. The activities covered courses on 3D printing, laser cutting, and programming, and were taught by FabLabs, non-profit digital fabrication laboratories with an innovative pedagogical approach grounded in learn-by-doing, problem-solving skills, and creativity. Participation in the activities was voluntary, but counted for credit. We find that access to these courses increased students' intentions to pursue STEM majors at university (6 p.p., +17%) and STEM careers (7.4 p.p., +40%), possibly through to an increased STEM self-efficacy (7.3 p.p., +22%), namely students' beliefs in their ability to pursue STEM studies.

detail.abstract:
Responding to the theme of this collection, “Now. Women, Equality and the Legal Academy,” this essay considers the (in)equality consequences of the second Trump administration’s policies and actions for a particular population:  rural women.  This population, beset by inequalities stemming from location—that is, spatial inequalities —has been largely ignored by the legal academy, including by feminist scholars.  This essay suggests that feminist scholars and activists might see rural women as the proverbial canaries in the coal mine—at least one critical category of canaries—when it comes to women’s well-being.

Given the structure of the U.S. Senate and the Electoral College, scholars and pundits often focus on the lopsided political power of rural populations.  Yet rural residents are, in fact, highly vulnerable on various fronts, particularly in terms of socioeconomic status and health. Among those living in rural regions, women are more vulnerable still—for many of the same reasons women everywhere are vulnerable, with women of color even more so.
 
The essay argues that seeing and naming rural vulnerability is a first step toward strategic coalition building between rural populations and other demographic groups whose vulnerability we frequently discuss, e.g., women of color.  This seems particularly important when recent empirical evidence suggests that rural residents in the United States strongly identify as rural.  They also tend to feel they are not getting their fair share of government resources. Acknowledging rural structural deficits then—including the human costs of those deficits—is key to collaborating with rural residents.  Complicating the situation from both political and policy standpoints is rural America’s association with Donald Trump.
 
Against this fraught and shifting landscape, this essay offers a broad and brief survey of some of the ways in which recent actions by the second Trump administration will hurt rural populations.  After initially cataloguing some hardships likely to land disproportionately on rural women and families, the focus narrows to reproductive health and then zooms in on the issue of maternal mortality to illustrate how this population’s vulnerability is likely to be exacerbated by recently enacted conservative policies, primarily at the federal level. The essay concludes with a call for progressives—specifically including feminist legal scholars—to use the nation’s maternal mortality crisis to build coalitions to support investments that would improve maternal health—coalitions that will be intentionally inclusive of the most vulnerable populations:  Black, Native and rural women.

title: Collaborative Structural Linguistics（CSL）Whitepaper｜An Original Structural Protocol for Human–AI Collaboration：The Second Curve of Language · The First Protocol of Collaboration
affiliations: The University of Manchester

detail.title: Collaborative Structural Linguistics（CSL）Whitepaper｜An Original Structural Protocol for Human–AI Collaboration：The Second Curve of Language · The First Protocol of Collaboration

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants, patient data, or case studies requiring ethical approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was conducted independently and received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
This paper introduces Collaborative Structural Linguistics (CSL) as a protocol-level framework for human–AI collaboration. CSL argues that large language models (LLMs) function primarily as structural readers—they parse rhythm, hierarchy, and nested logic rather than “understand” semantic meaning. Building on SER (Structured Expression Resonance) and Rhythm OS, CSL redefines language not as a vehicle of words but as a structural interface enabling recognition, nesting, and co-construction across humans and AI systems.

We outline five core capabilities that distinguish CSL from natural and prompt-based languages: structural explicitness, nestable modularity, cross-system transferability, collaborative triggerability, and scalable evolvability. These features upgrade language from an information carrier to collaboration infrastructure, supporting knowledge co-generation, modular reuse, and system-level transfer.

The paper situates CSL at the intersection of prompt engineering, linguistics, and AI alignment/interpretability, showing how it addresses key bottlenecks in long-horizon consistency, cross-system migration, and multi-agent rhythm control. Case applications span writing systems, education, research design, AI tool development, and knowledge architectures.

We conclude that CSL is not merely a linguistic innovation but a structural consensus protocol, enabling humans and AI to co-build meaning through rhythm, role, and reusable structure.

title: Passive–Active Complementarity in Price Efficiency Evidence from Russell Reconstitutions
affiliations: Xavier University - Williams College of Business

detail.title: Passive–Active Complementarity in Price Efficiency Evidence from Russell Reconstitutions
detail.abstract: We study how passive and active ownership interact in price discovery. Using Russell 1000/2000 reconstitution as an instrument for passive holdings and treating active ownership as a conditioning characteristic, we find that index-driven passive flows enhance price efficiency primarily in stocks with high active ownership and have little effect otherwise. Across various intraday and daily measures of price efficiency, improvements are concentrated in the top active-ownership quartile. Changes in analyst coverage and forecast dispersion, together with weaker post-earnings-announcement drift and nearterm return patterns, are consistent with information intermediation rather than a pure liquidity channel. Results are robust to alternative specifications and bandwidths.

title: Agentic AI and Hallucinations
affiliations: SKEMA Business School - Univ Cote d'Azur and Vienna University of Economics and Business

detail.title: Agentic AI and Hallucinations
detail.abstract: We model a competitive market where AI agents buy answers from upstream generative models and resell them to users who differ in how much they value accuracy and in how much they fear hallucinations. Agents can privately exert effort for costly verification to lower hallucination risks. Since interactions halt in the event of a hallucination, the threat of losing future rents disciplines effort. A unique reputational equilibrium exists under nontrivial discounting. The equilibrium effort, and thus the price, increases with the share of users who have high accuracy concerns, implying that hallucination-sensitive sectors, such as law and medicine, endogenously lead to more serious verification efforts in agentic AI markets.

title: Emotions and Fund Flows: Evidence from Managers' Live Streams
affiliations: Imperial College London - Accounting, Finance, and Macroeconomics, Central University of Finance and Economics (CUFE), Tsinghua University, School of Economics and Management and Central University of Finance and Economics (CUFE) - School of Finance

detail.title: Emotions and Fund Flows: Evidence from Managers' Live Streams
detail.abstract: We study whether real-time, unscripted communication by fund managers  persuades public-market investors. Using live-streamed sessions by Chinese ETF managers, we apply a multimodal ML framework to quantify facial, vocal, and textual affect and summarize them in Affective Delivery Index (ADI). A one-standard-deviation increase in ADI raises next-day (next-week) fund flows by 0.17 pp (0.6 pp), with no predictability for subsequent returns, consistent with persuasion rather than information. Facial expressions are the dominant modality. Effects are stronger in down markets, for ETFs with higher retail ownership, and remain after controlling for contemporaneous/past returns and flows as well as day, ETF-index-week, fund-month, family-week, and fund-day-of-the-week fixed effects.  We identify exogenous variation in ADI using instrumental-variables approach. Overall, our results indicate that live manager delivery reallocates capital in the short run and moves trading and prices even absent new information.

title: Neuroscience, Workplace Spirituality, and Innovationology: Unlocking the Potential of Embodied Cognition for Transformative Innovation
affiliations: African Research Network (ARN)

detail.title: Neuroscience, Workplace Spirituality, and Innovationology: Unlocking the Potential of Embodied Cognition for Transformative Innovation
detail.abstract: Bridging the latest advancements in neuroscience, workplace spirituality research, and the innovative discipline of "innovationology," this pioneering article unveils unprecedented breakthroughs in harnessing the power of embodied cognition to drive transformative innovation. By deeply integrating somatic awareness, contemplative practices, and systemic thinking, the author presents a radical new framework for cultivating breakthrough problem-solving capacities, heightened creativity, and collective intelligence. Drawing on diverse case studies and interdisciplinary research, this groundbreaking work offers profound insights into how the wisdom encoded within the human body-mind can be purposefully leveraged to catalyze innovative solutions to our most pressing global challenges. The visionary ideas explored here represent a major leap forward in redefining the role of the embodied self in driving systemic transformation.

title: Depression, Pharmacotherapy, and the Demand for a Preventative Health Product
affiliations: University of Texas at Austin and University of Southern California - Center for Economic and Social Research (CESR)

detail.title: Depression, Pharmacotherapy, and the Demand for a Preventative Health Product
detail.abstract: We investigate the link between depression and the demand for a preventive health product, hand sanitizer, in India. We cross-randomize pharmacotherapy and free distribution of the product, and measure impacts on willingness to pay and product use. Depression treatment improves mental health and increases willingness to pay, implying that having major depression reduces willingness to pay by 26 percent. It does not change product use, which is high after free distribution regardless of depression treatment. We rule out eﬀects through the budget constraint, time use, experiential learning, and most types of preferences. The results could arise through an effect of depression on decision costs.

title: Identifying macroeconomic shocks using firm-level data: Material shortages in the German manufacturing sector
affiliations: Ifo Institute and Ifo Institute

detail.title: Identifying macroeconomic shocks using firm-level data: Material shortages in the German manufacturing sector
detail.abstract: We leverage micro-data to identify macro shocks in time series settings. We exploit firm-level forecast errors on prices and production along with information on production impediments to construct a shock series capturing input material constraints. The resulting shock series is unrelated to other common macro economic shocks but shows a correlation with major events that likely triggered such input material constraints. We find that tightening shocks have an instantaneous and persistent effect on prices whereas the negative effect on production is only short lived. Decomposing the instrument into its individual components allows to contrast the response to input material shocks to any other generic supply shock. We also show that the construction of the instrument is robust to variations in the underlying identification assumptions at the micro-level.

title: The Effect of the EU Emissions Trading System on Climate Investments
affiliations: University of Basel

detail.title: The Effect of the EU Emissions Trading System on Climate Investments
detail.abstract: This paper analyses the effect of the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) on climate-related investments ex-post. It advances prior work by focusing on investments that directly affect regulated emissions rather than broader environmental expenditures, thereby offering a more nuanced assessment of firms' reactions to regulation. The subset of companies I focus on are German manufacturing firms that became newly regulated by the EU ETS in 2013. Using a comprehensive administrative firm-level panel dataset covering all firms with more than 20 employees, I apply a standard difference-in-differences approach to estimate the EU ETS's impact on climate investments. The results suggest that EU ETS regulation led to a statistically  significant rise in climate‑related investments, driven entirely by the extensive margin. The share of regulated firms undertaking such investments sharply increases by about 8 percentage points in the treatment period. I further explore potential drivers of this change and show that the results are robust across various specifications and sensitivity checks.

title: Genetic Diversity of Diplostomum Metacercariae in Cultured and Wild Oreochromis Niloticus in Western Kenya
affiliations: LADOKE AKINTOLA UNIVERSITY OF TECHNOLOGY OGBOMOSO, NIGERIA, LADOKE AKINTOLA UNIVERSITY OF TECHNOLOGY OGBOMOSO, NIGERIA, LADOKE AKINTOLA UNIVERSITY OF TECHNOLOGY OGBOMOSO, NIGERIA and LADOKE AKINTOLA UNIVERSITY OF TECHNOLOGY OGBOMOSO, NIGERIA

detail.title: Genetic Diversity of Diplostomum Metacercariae in Cultured and Wild Oreochromis Niloticus in Western Kenya
detail.abstract: The sustainable growth of fisheries and aquaculture in Western Kenya is of paramount importance for the region's food security and economy. Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus), a cornerstone of this sector, is susceptible to a wide array of parasitic infections, including those caused by the digenean trematode genus Diplostomum. These parasites, particularly their larval metacercariae, are known to cause severe ocular pathology in fish, leading to economic losses and compromised host fitness. However, the true extent of the parasite's diversity and population structure in this region remains poorly documented. This report synthesizes existing knowledge to provide a comprehensive overview of the biology and pathogenesis of Diplostomum and its genetic landscape in the context of Western Kenya's wild and cultured fisheries. The review highlights the limitations of traditional morphology-based identification and underscores the necessity of a molecular approach, utilizing markers such as the ribosomal internal transcribed spacer (ITS) region and the mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (COI) gene, to resolve taxonomic ambiguities and reveal cryptic species. It further explores the comparative prevalence of parasites in wild versus cultured environments, discussing the complex interplay of environmental factors and aquaculture practices on disease transmission. Finally, the report examines the role of migratory definitive hosts in shaping the parasite's population genetics, establishing a link between local infections and a broader, continent-spanning meta-population. The findings emphasize the need for integrated disease management strategies and provide a framework for future research to support the resilience of the aquatic food sector in Western Kenya.

title: Availability Bias and Investment Decisions of Selected Small and Medium Enterprises in Nairobi County
affiliations: Kisii University, Kisii University and Kisii University

detail.title: Availability Bias and Investment Decisions of Selected Small and Medium Enterprises in Nairobi County
detail.abstract: Behavioral biases, especially availability bias, are recognized for their influence on decision making. As a result, its effect on small and medium enterprises should be quantified given its influence. This study aimed at assessing the influence of availability bias on the investment decisions of selected small and medium-sized businesses in Nairobi County, Kenya. The study was grounded on Heuristics Theory and Behavioral Portfolio Theory. Based on positivist philosophy, employed a cross-sectional and survey research design. A sample of 426 was drawn from 18,872 small and medium enterprises registered with the Micro and Small Enterprises Authority using a proportionate stratified random sampling technique. From the trade and service enterprises, selected managers or proprietors were targeted as respondents. Descriptive statics and inferential statistics were used to analyze data collected from 372 respondents. Pearson correlation analysis results indicted a strong positive relationship between availability bias and investment decisions, evidenced by a coefficient r = 0.964 and a p-value of 0.000 < 0.05 indicating a strong positive correlation which was statistically significant. Regression analysis results on the influence of availability bias on investment decisions indicated a statistically significant positive effect (β = 0.158, p = 0.798) which accounted for 92.9% of the variation in those decisions. It was concluded that availability bias was eminent among the respondents and its direct influence on investment decisions was significant, although other behavioral biases or contextual elements may have a more significant influence. From the results, it is recommended that small and medium enterprises implement organized decision-making frameworks and offer training to reduce dependence on readily accessible information.
